description:
🍋 Lemon Meringue Pie Ice Cream – The most AMAZING, Tangiest Scoop! 🍨🔥

If you love lemon meringue pie, this recipe turns it into the ultimate ice cream experience. An updated version of my FIRST EVER Youtube video all those years ago. Fresh dairy, silky texture, and that unmistakable lemony punch—with no egg yolks needed. Perfectly smooth, bright, sweet, and nostalgic.

👇 Full Recipe Below
👇 Timestamps Included
👇 Use this to WOW your friends, kids, neighbours or even some random stranger you want to give ice cream to 😂

⸻

🕒 TIMESTAMPS

00:00 – Intro & Breakdown
01:35 – Ingredients for base
02:25 – Making the ice cream base
04:56 – Making the Pie Crust add in
08:11 – Making the Meringuey bit
11:25 – Loading up stage
12:12 – Scoop and Reveal
14:33 – Outro and Next week

⸻

🧪 INGREDIENTS
 • 592g Whole Milk (3.25%)
 • 582g Heavy Cream (33%)
 • 230g Sugar
 • 24g Invert Sugar or Corn Syrup
 • 65g SMP (skim milk powder)
 • 6–10g Lemon Extract (adjust strength to taste)

Add-Ins:
Cubed or Crumbled Graham pie crust:
200g Graham Crumb
100g Butter

Meringue swirl (toast it for more flavour):
100g Egg Whites (not yolks 😂)
100g Sugar
30g Corn Syrup or Glucose
1.5g Cream of Tartar

⸻

⭐ WHAT MAKES THIS SPECIAL

✨ High SMP for dense, creamy body
✨ Balanced sugars for scoopability
✨ Bright lemon extract without acidity curdling dairy
✨ Stable texture even after freezing
✨ Perfect add ins for both textur and flavour

This recipe is designed to give you that pie-filling flavor with creamy dairy richness. Add a layer of  meringue and you’re in dessert heaven.

⸻

🔑 KEYWORDS & TAGS

comments.text: So in this recipe you added the zest, in the orange ice cream video you boiled the skin. My question is, would oleo saccharum work? Is there a reason you don't use it?
comments.author: @ssl666

comments.text: It would work yes. I don’t use but u don’t make enough of those flavours. TBH I don’t think many folk would be able to tell the difference between one made with zest, extract or oleo saccharum. As long as you balance the sugars correctly
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  So why not save quite a lot of time and just zest/boil and be done. Thanks for the reply, love the content! <3
comments.author: @ssl666

comments.text: @ssl666  I think your idea of time saving is different to mine...Zest and done. No messing about, it's the fastest way. You do it your way of you like.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: Oh, man, Nick. This was such a timely recipe! My grandson was just asking me to make a lemon meringue ice cream and I was ready to hunt down a recipe. Then, voila, this appeared on my feed. I just finished assembling it and it's perfection. The volume of this recipe exceeded my Cuisinart churner, so I just made it in 2 batches. I'll proportionately reduce it in the future. I didn't see your stabilizer volume, so used 3g. I also used a delicious Swiss meringue from a different recipe of yours (which did not include invert sugar, since I couldn't discern the volume you used in this recipe). I did toast the meringue with a kitchen torch (oh man, so good), but the biggest variant for me (due to an aversion in the family for graham cracker crusts) was the generous use of shards of frozen baked real pie crust interspersed in the assembly.  This lemon ice cream was phenomenal. It's going on our list of fav's for sure!
comments.author: @Zandertunz

comments.text: I’ve never made it with normal pie crust but definitely want to. Thank you for the feedback and I’ve usually got a tub of this in the freezer myself 😂🤤
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: FYI, for the pie crust element, I used a frozen unbaked sheet of pie crust from Trader Joe's, which is a sturdy dough (not too flakey).  I cut the sheet into shards and bake them on a silpat on a cookie sheet. Once cooled, I place them in a plastic container in the freezer to use for just this purpose.  When assembling the ice cream, I do not add the crust to the churn, but layer it ala "Hello My Name is Ice Cream" layering technique, alternating between randomly sprinkled shards of pie crust, lemon ice cream and toasted meringue.  The pie crust layers add such a great buttery note to the bite, it's distinctly different than the graham cracker crust (which I have also made per your instructions for other ice creams, eg. Key Lime Pie). The result is actually kind of luxurious and authentically pie-esque.  I think you'll love it.
comments.author: @Zandertunz

comments.text:
i made a meringue based ice cream a week ago cause i couldnt get my pavlova meringue to hold its shape, looked just like your meringue. my swiss meringue was 100g~ separated egg whites with 170g~ of sugar, with 1 cup of heavy cream.

i beat the heavy cream into whipped cream and added a splash of vanilla extract. to my meringue i added almond extract to give it a cherry flavor, i also made a berry compote for my pav so i had to use it for my ice cream.

once i had my whipped cream and collapsed meringue i folded them together along with the berry compote. the ice cream was incredibly soft and scooped like soft gelato. the berry compote was a nice contrast to the meringue and the almond extract brought in a nice flavor depth without being too different from the flavor profile.

im going to make a key lime pie ice cream, so im thinking on making the lime custard and whipping the custard to fold into the meringue (saves me from more dirty dishes). i plan to add the graham cubes to the ice cream just to make it a bit more boujee and add some flavor depth and texture to the ice cream.
